newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Mammoth cocaine haul made in Pacific off Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Mammoth cocaine haul made in Pacific off Colombia.

text.p: An international anti-drug force made the biggest high-seas cocaine seizure on record off Colombia's Pacific coast, Col. Leonardo Gallego, chief of the country's anti-drug police, said on Wednesday.

At least seven tonnes of cocaine was found on Tuesday on a 635-tonne fishing boat bound for the Mexican port of Manzanillo. Gallego said at least 4.5 tonnes, and possibly as much as seven tonnes, was still concealed in fuel tanks on board, according to intelligence reports.

Colombian and Ecuadorian police, together with U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration agents, took part in the joint operation, dubbed Operation Shark. One Colombian and four Ecuadorians were arrested, and the vessel was towed to the Ecuadorian port of Esmeraldas.
Gallego said the shipment probably belonged to a new gang of traffickers made up of survivors of the largely dismantled Medellin and Cali cartels, in league with Mexican drug lords.
A Colombian police spokesman said small launches had loaded the cocaine cargo onto the Ecuadorian-registered fishing boat off Colombia's Pacific coast.
DEA agents estimate Colombia supplies 80 percent of the world's cocaine. The country's drug cartels are also becoming major players in the high-grade heroin market.
